cora: Heads up — seeing ~20% p50 throughput regression on nf4-prod after yesterday's prefetch heuristic change. Dash: https://perf.redwood/internal/d/abc123/nf4-prod

vinod: Which model/batch/profile? any kernel selector logs?

cora: model=redwood/llama-13b-nf4, mix of seq lengths 512/1024, client batch sizes 1-8. Spike shows up as increased tail of host memcpy + GPU kernel slowpath for 4-bit kernels. Attached selector snippet below.

cora: ```
[2026-03-17T03:12:10Z] kernel_selector: model=llama-13b-nf4 seq=512 batch=4 -> selected=q4_prefetch_v2 (prefetch_window=64)
[2026-03-17T03:12:10Z] kernel_executor: executing=q4_prefetch_v2 kernel_ms=4.8
[2026-03-17T03:12:10Z] kernel_executor: fallback=slow_conv_ms=9.2 (triggered_when=host_kv_miss>0.12)
```

cora: perf counters (short): KV_cache_miss_rate jumped from 0.03->0.18, host_memcpy_bytes/sec +60%, scheduler wait_ns +30%.

perf-bot: ALERT: throughput_drop detected on cluster nf4-prod (20.3%). Correlated deploy: prefetch-heuristic:v2 @ 2440001000.

sylvia: :eyes: I think prefetch_window=64 may be overshooting for mixed-length traces. Prefetch floods host->GPU copies and triggers intermediate slowpath when device queues cross threshold. Can we try window=32 or adaptive cutoff?

kevin: Can we repro in staging? I can run a replay harness (replay + perf counters) if you give a trace.

cora: Pushed a small trace to staging (s3://redwood-tests/nf4/traces/244000-trace-1) — it's pretty representative. Repro steps below.

cora: ```bash
# run replay on staging node with perf hooks
./tools/replay_trace --trace s3://redwood-tests/nf4/traces/244000-trace-1 --kernel-override=q4_prefetch_v2 --collect-perf=true --runs=120
```

vinod: I ran 3 iterations locally. Observed same memcpy spike when prefetch_window>=48. With prefetch_window=32 we don't cross the KV miss threshold and slowpath doesn't trigger. Logs: host_memcpy_ms drop from 6.1->2.5, device_queue_depth stays <120.

sylvia: That matches an analysis I did on prefetch alignment: when prefetch overlaps with concurrent KV fetches it creates bursts that increase host-to-device memcpy contention. The kernel selector fallback check uses an absolute host_kv_miss rate which is now sensitive to burstiness rather than sustained miss rate.

kevin: Quick mitigation: toggle prefetch-heuristic=v1 feature flag for prod to restore previous behavior while we deploy a fix. Also add a moving-window based miss-rate metric instead of instantaneous threshold.

cora: Rolled flag toggle in prod to prefetch-heuristic:v1 at 2440001210. Early check shows p50 back to baseline (~+1% vs prior).

sylvia: Good. Long-term fixes: 1) adaptive prefetch_window that shrinks when host memcpy latency rises; 2) kernel_selector change: use burst-aware miss rate (EWMA over 10s) for fallback decision; 3) instrumentation: emit prefetch_batch_size and host_memcpy_latency per request.

vinod: I'll open a bisect PR that adds a regression test around mixed-length trace and asserts no >10% p50 regression when comparing v1 vs v2. Also add a perf test for prefetch_window param grid.

kevin: I'll schedule a canary with window=32 + ewma-based fallback to validate perf before re-enabling full rollout.

cora: Action items summarized:
- vinod: PR with bisect/test + perf harness (due EOD 3/18)
- sylvia: design doc for adaptive prefetch and ewma fallback (draft by 3/19)
- kevin: canary plan + roll flag until fix is in (start canary 3/19)
- infra: add telemetry fields (prefetch_window, host_memcpy_p50) to per-request trace (ticket INF-4872)

cora: Thanks all — leaving prod flag in v1 for now. Will update thread with bisect results. :thumbsup:
